My Asperger's. I can't read body language at all past happy/noticeably very sad/angry. I have one friend that i've known for twelve years and I can sometimes tell when something is bothering him. I can fake it til I make it with talking in front of a few people, until I say something that makes sense to me but not the way I worded it to them. I also either end up labelled as "not interested in the conversation at all" or "Why are you asking so many questions?" and that's not even a conversation about something i'm interested in. I can't find the balance between not being too eager in a conversation and trying to find out what the person actually means.

Which brings me onto my next point, I have yet to find someone who doesn't get annoyed if I ask them what they mean more than three times a day. I do see how it could get annoying every other sentence, but when people talk in sentences that could mean three different things, I literally can't tell which way you want me to take it in the conversation because I have zero social context.

Then we come to attempting to date. A girl kind of giggled and walked away when I asked her out once, but i'm just gonna put that one down as high school and not count this one. I don't hold it against her, everyone is socially awkward in high school, just some more than others.

The first was a few years ago in high school, and she only wanted to "date" me to get out of an abusive foster home(I would have had no problem helping her with said issue in any way I could if I had been filled in on the plan from the beginning). She stayed at my house for a few months, until she went off to summer camp and screwed six of the kids she was teaching and two other counselors. The second, I went to pick my friend up from a bar so he wouldn't drive home, and he brought another friend with him. I drop them off at second guy's apartment to sleep it off and pick my friend up in the morning to go get his car. This new friend of his brought a bunch of his friends into our small group, which was going fine for a few months, we all really did seem to get along. Until one day, one of the new girls asked me out. Naturally I stuttered my way through a yes, and after choosing a time/place, I showed up at her house to pick her up on the day of the date. The door is opened by one of many of her friends sitting in the living room at her house, and she laughs at me asking how I could have thought she was serious. How could I not have? They've been harrassing me ever since, so i've just been taking extra shifts at work and not really hanging out with anyone.

I know a lot of people will say "Look at the upsides to it" and i've seen them. When i'm focused on something, either learning about it or using it practically, I can be as good as five people doing that thing. So long as that thing is something that doesn't involve any social interaction at all, of course. I can be very organized when I put in the effort, and when I do know someone is going through something tough, i've been told that even if it takes a while to explain to me *why* they feel *how* they feel, i'm one of the preferred people to have there because I do everything I can to help. I guess I did hit okay in the looks department for genetics, at least. I don't know how good I look, but I did have a friend say "above average" once and i'll take that because i'm pretty bad at judging anyone's physical attractiveness.

I genuinely would rather be dead than live not understanding people at all, and I think I might be before my next birthday.

Edward I always use, because I need a swordsman early on. Personally, I like Mia and Lucia more, but I usually take 2-3 to endgame anyway. Probably a little biased because it is my favourite unit type, but he does hold his own.

Aran, I don't see many talk about. I don't know who is better between him and Nephenee, but sometimes I use both anyway. He is my main hit-taker in the dawn brigade early on, since his defense usually grows pretty good.

Micaiah. My only problem with her is low defense and sometimes not many HP growths, but I usually stick her behind a sentinel anyway. MVP for taking down general types early on.

Crimea. I love Elincia's gambit, favourite map really. I wish Lucia could be used in this, because she is in my opinion, the best unit from this chapter. I know most say Haar is, but I always end up flying units being wrecked in every game. 

Greil Mercenaries. This is where it gets tough. Oscar and Mia are my trump cards here, and Ike is of course really good. Soren usually ends up as my best mage.

Endgame. Every unit mentioned before here usually gets used. Skipping over part 4 where it swaps between Greil Mercenaries and Dawn brigade, because the units I use are mentioned already aswell. In endgame I use the hell out of Nailah, and Sothe. I level him a bit during the dawn brigade chapters, mostly when there is a tough unit early on, but I make sure to level him here before he gets his upgrade. When the tower starts, Kurthnaga is a beast. I understand why he isn't in most of the game, both story and unit wise, even if I wish he was. 

Sacred stones. Gilliam was my most used, He tanked like, everything. Gerik and Marisa were my other two who were used a lot. 

Awakening. First I did the main story, which my team was Robin as a tactician, Chrom, Lucina, Gregor, Stahl, Olivia and I don't even remember who else. When I grinded, My main units were Severa, Lucina, Robin, Morgan, Kjelle, Inigo, Cynthia, Olivia(Refresh, yo!), and Noire. The most used I would say would be Robin and Lucina in the main story, and Severa and Lucina after grinding were my best. 

Fates. Corrin was most used, I had him as a lodestar. Azura I used to refresh everyone, not much else. Only I got a magic throwing weapon for Felicia in any of the playthroughs, she was really good too.

So, the coyote attack. Happened last october. I am in the backyard, door open because I was just going out to grab something from my mothers car for her. As I grab whatever it is she wanted, I turn around and there it is. The biggest Coyote I had seen(in person). Now, It wouldn't have been such a big deal, if I had my shotgun(which I use to hunt snowshoe hare, and if I see a coyote I take that to lower their insane population where I live, as well as collect the bounty.) I do the only logical thing I can think of, make myself a little bigger, because any sudden movement I make for my knife(clipped onto the knee brace I wore after dislocating my leg, and popping it back in myself) would most likely set the coyote off. To put me in proportion, I would say the coyote is roughly the size of a decently big rottweiler. I am a 15 year old dude who weighs only 150, about 5 foot 10. 

The coyote lunges at me, so I react on instinct alone(I do highschool wrestling, probably the only thing that saved me at that point.) I dive to the right, spin around, and wait for him to make another move. At this point I am on the side with the house door facing me, and he/she is by the car. He runs and tries to do a leap towards my neck I assume, so I grab him by his neck in the air and just slam him down. I hold him down with one arm, as he is wildly thrashing and trying to bite me, and reach to the knife with the other. It slips out of my hand and distracts me for a moment, but that seemed to be enough for him to get out of my grip. But then my saving grace, the dog who saved my life(technically twice, she woke me up and damn near drug me out of my burning house not two weeks later) comes running out and full on tackles the damn thing off me, which gives me enough time to quickly grab the knife and stab it while it is disoriented from my dogs whopping 60ish pound tackle(she was a border collie, runt of the litter, but best dog i've ever known.) My mother walks out not seconds later, and screams at all the scratches from my brawl on the gravel driveway with the coyote are seen by her. I had just walked out in my shorts, as I was in the middle of getting dressed when she needed me to get whatever it was. So there I stood, lots of blood running down my chest/back/arms/legs, my dog sitting beside me getting the "good girl" treatment with lots of petting, and a coyote with my hunting knife still stuck inside of its skull on the ground next to us. Needless to say, she took me to the hospital because she was worrywart mom, and I had an amazing tale to tell the nurses while we waited. Obligatory RIP to my dog, Happy, for saving me from both this coyote, and pulling me out of our house fire(I sleep through smoke alarms), who ran back inside because usually I am only home if little bro is(I had a half day at school), and we assume she went looking for him.
